_Requested by **Sure Team** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VhYV3jhQ9s4qrrh2th12sN?thread=cmsg_01VhYV3jhQ9s4qrrh2th12sNJ8kbdRnDAGUoNgmGPAc9wq)_

Item: obs-journal-vs-world

## What

- `packages/journal/bin/journal-check.js` + `src/check.js`: one command that compares the journal with
  - a session's own event log (saved `list_events` pages, or the Claude Code transcript and its subagents), listing tool calls with no `tool.call` row and rows whose call the log doesn't have;
  - GitHub's closed PRs (REST, through the session proxy, or saved responses with `--prs`), listing merges with no `pr.merge` row (with head and merge sha) and `pr.merge` rows GitHub doesn't bear out.
  - `--record` appends a `journal.check` row with the counts. Exit 0 clean, 1 gaps, 2 can't run.
- Capture writes a `pr.merge` row when the GitHub MCP merge tool's own response says merged (shape recorded from scratch PR #11).
- New kinds `pr.merge`, `journal.check`; docs/journal.md "The journal check"; decision `plan/decisions/2026-10-30-journal-check.md`.

## Builder's runs (not the proof)

- Headless `claude -p --plugin-dir plugins/harness` session (5 calls incl. a subagent): 0 missing; after deleting one `tool.call` row in a copy, exactly that call is listed.
- This thread (release 0.1.0, no capture) against its transcript: 37 of 37 finished calls missing, which is true. Real GitHub: 14 merges since 16:00Z in both repos, all listed (no session has captured a merge yet).
- `npm test`: 176 pass, 2 fail — both `cheap` timing tests (median 52–53 ms vs 50), which fail the same on main in this container.

The verifier proves the Expect lines in a separate session.

commit.message:
obs-journal-vs-world: check the journal against session logs and GitHub

journal-check.js compares a session's tool.call rows with its own event log (saved list_events
pages or the Claude Code transcript) and the journal's pr.merge rows with GitHub's merged PRs, and
lists missing calls, merges with no journal row, and rows the world doesn't bear out. Capture now
writes pr.merge from the GitHub MCP merge tool's response. The item is marked done, effective when
the verdict merges.

+## The journal check
+
+`packages/journal/bin/journal-check.js` (plan item obs-journal-vs-world) compares the journal with facts from
+outside it and lists what doesn't match (ledger L-checks-against-world). It reads and never repairs: a gap stays a
+gap until a separate, explicit command writes a labelled placeholder row.
+
+```
+node packages/journal/bin/journal-check.js --journal <session file> --events <event log>
+node packages/journal/bin/journal-check.js --journal <journal root> --repo <owner/name> [--since <ISO time>]
+```
+
+- **Session diff** (`--events`, with `--session <file>` when `--journal` is the root). The event log is the
+  session's own record of its tool calls: `list_events` pages saved as JSON or JSONL, or a Claude Code transcript
+  (its `subagents/` folder is read too). It lists every call that ran with no `tool.call` row, and every
+  `tool.call` row inside the log's time span whose tool use id the log doesn't have. Calls Claude Code answered
+  without running (a `<tool_use_error>` result, such as a blocked `sleep`) and calls with no result yet are shown
+  but not counted: no hook fires for them. `list_events` is an MCP tool, so the session saves its pages to a file
+  first; a cloud session's local transcript is under `~/.claude/projects/`.
+- **Merge diff** (`--repo`, repeatable). It asks GitHub's REST API for the repo's closed PRs (through the session's
+  proxy, which Node needs `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` for; the command sets it) or reads saved responses with `--prs`. It
+  lists every PR merged since `--since` (default: the journal's first row) with no `pr.merge` row naming it, with
+  its head and merge shas, and every `pr.merge` row GitHub shows unmerged or merged at another sha. A merge made
+  through the REST API, the web UI or `git push` has no `pr.merge` row, so it is listed (case
+  C-merge-outside-host-detected). Until the engine's merge effect exists, a merge with the GitHub MCP merge tool
+  in a session that captures counts as journalled.
+- `--record <file>` appends a `journal.check` row: `payload` has `ok`, `since`, `journal`, the counts (`calls`,
+  `callRows`, `missing`, `notRun`, `pending`, `unfoundCalls`, `outside`, `merges`, `mergeRows`, `unexplained`,
+  `unfoundMerges`) and `badLines`, the journal lines it couldn't read.
+- Exit 0 when nothing is listed, 1 when something is, 2 when it couldn't run. `--json` prints the whole result.
+
+`list_events` retention is unknown, so run the session diff soon after a session ends.
+

+# The journal check reads saved event logs, and a merge is journalled by a pr.merge row from capture
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-30, by the obs-journal-vs-world thread, on the person's standing instruction to decide two-way
+doors and not wait.
+
+**Event log as a file.** The item names `list_events` as the session's own record. That is an MCP tool, which a
+command can't call, so `journal-check.js --events` reads `list_events` pages a session saved, or a Claude Code
+transcript, which holds the same tool_use and tool_result blocks (and its `subagents/` folder holds the subagents').
+Both shapes give the same calls (`packages/journal/test/check.test.js`).
+
+**Calls no hook sees aren't counted missing.** A call Claude Code answers without running (a `<tool_use_error>`
+result, such as a blocked `sleep`) fires no hook (seen by the obs-live-capture verifier), so no capture can journal
+it. The report shows these, and calls with no result yet, but leaves them out of "missing" and of the exit code.
+
+**What journals a merge.** Nothing recorded merges before this item, and tool.call rows keep only a hash of the
+input, so the check couldn't tell a journalled merge from any other. Capture now writes a `pr.merge` row when the
+GitHub MCP merge tool's own response says merged: `owner/repo#number` and GitHub's merge sha, the one place capture
+keeps tool-input identifiers. A merge through the REST API, the web UI or `git push` has no such row and is listed
+(case C-merge-outside-host-detected). When engine-effects builds the host's merge effect, it can narrow "journalled"
+to its own rows. Reversible: the rule lives in `checkMerges()`.
+
+**GitHub through the proxy.** Node's fetch ignores `HTTPS_PROXY` unless `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` is set, and the cloud
+session reaches api.github.com only through its proxy (403 without it, 200 with it, 2026-10-30), so the command runs
+itself again with it set. Repo-scoped REST reads work with the proxy's credentials; no token is needed.
+
+**Where the check row goes.** `--record <file>` appends the `journal.check` row to the file the caller names,
+usually its own session file, so one writer per file holds.
+
+**What a real session in the v2 project can show today.** Thread sessions still run release 0.1.0, which has no
+capture (their self-check says so), so their journals have no tool.call rows and the check lists every call as
+missing; that is a true report. A captured real session needs a thread on 0.1.3 or later, or a headless
+`claude -p --plugin-dir plugins/harness` session, as obs-live-capture's verifier used.
